sections.churn_summary: Hold-buffer guards are live on all three focus tracks (`exit_confirm_screens`: 2, `reentry_cooldown_screens`: 1, `min_rebalance_notional_gbp`: 10.0), but none are actively buffering exits: `buffered_holdings` is 0 and `exit_streak` is empty everywhere. Cost drag remains elevated on the active churn tracks—rules 29.0% (`cost_drag`: 0.2897, `trade_count`: 48) and primary ai_judgment 21.2% (`cost_drag`: 0.2125, `trade_count`: 29)—while momentum_grace sits at 2.9% (`cost_drag`: 0.0291, `trade_count`: 5) with zero trades in the last 7d. The buffered-hold counterfactual shows `exit_confirm_screens`=2 materially reduces churn on rules (`trade_count_delta_lower_minus_higher`: 3, `cost_drag_delta_lower_minus_higher`: 0.0856) but barely moves ai_judgment (`trade_count_delta_lower_minus_higher`: 1, `cost_drag_delta_lower_minus_higher`: 0.0006). The single biggest operational learning gap is that the primary ai_judgment track just applied `min_conviction` 0.45 (`applied`: true) yet has `post_apply_trade_count`: 0, `equity_marks`: 0, and `benchmark_span_available`: false—so the knob epoch cannot yet be evaluated against ^FTSE.

sections.proposed_experiments:
1. [paper_churn] Rules track exit_confirm_screens=1 vs 2 extended replay — quantify whether the 7d window finding (`cost_drag_delta_lower_minus_higher` 0.0856, 3 fewer trades at screens=2) holds over rules' full epoch (`post_apply_trade_count` 13, 7 equity marks) before any guard change.
2. [paper_churn] ai_judgment min_rebalance_notional_gbp sweep (£10 baseline vs £25/£50 in track config.json) — test whether small rebalance legs driving 29 lifetime trades and 21.2% cost drag can be throttled without waiting for epoch marks on the new min_conviction 0.45 setting.
3. [offline_sim] IMB.L adjacent-flip root-cause replay across rules + ai_judgment — both tracks logged 1 adjacent buy→sell flip on IMB.L with `reentry_cooldown` {"IMB.L": 1}; replay with `reentry_cooldown_screens` 1 vs 2 to learn if cooldown length would have blocked the whipsaw.
